entries.name: Run every N ticks
entries.summary: Start this block at a fixed interval measured in game ticks.
entries.details: 20 ticks is one second at 20 TPS. This creates a trigger; it is not a delay inside another block.
entries.placementHelp: Outside other blocks.
entries.argumentsHelp: Choose a positive integer interval. Tick intervals use game ticks; 20 ticks is one game second. Offset changes phase, not frequency.

entries.name: Run every N seconds
entries.summary: Start this block at a fixed interval measured in game seconds.
entries.details: One game second is 20 ticks; server lag can make real-world seconds longer.
entries.placementHelp: Outside other blocks.
entries.argumentsHelp: Choose a positive integer interval. Tick intervals use game ticks; 20 ticks is one game second. Offset changes phase, not frequency.

entries.name: Run on the world clock
entries.summary: Run at a fixed interval using the world clock and a chosen offset.
entries.details: The offset changes the starting phase, not the interval. Managers using the same settings can run together.
entries.placementHelp: Outside other blocks.
entries.argumentsHelp: Choose a positive integer interval. Tick intervals use game ticks; 20 ticks is one game second. Offset changes phase, not frequency.

entries.name: Spread timer start times
entries.summary: Give managers random starting offsets while keeping a fixed interval.
entries.details: The offset is sampled once per activation, not after every run. This header currently requires Code.
entries.insert:
every 20 plus (RANDOM(0, 19)) ticks do
  print("running")
end
entries.placementHelp: Outside other blocks.
entries.argumentsHelp: Choose a positive integer interval. Tick intervals use game ticks; 20 ticks is one game second. Offset changes phase, not frequency.

entries.name: When the Manager receives a pulse
entries.summary: Start this block when the Factory Manager detects a redstone pulse.

firstSuccess.title: Move your first items
steps: Have a Factory Manager, program disk, Label Gun, SFM cable, two single chests, and a Programming Station for this Studio workflow. Connect the Manager and both chests on the same cable network.

Right-click the Label Gun in air. Create/select source, then right-click the supplying chest once and read chat confirmation. Open the gun in air again, choose dest, and label the empty receiving chest. Clicking an already assigned chest again can remove the label.
Put eight test items in source. Hold one fresh blank SFM disk, then open the Programming Station. Choose the complete two-chest example as a new draft, then Save and Check it.
In Build revisions choose Publish saved, select that build, and choose Imprint disk. Close Studio and insert the imprinted disk into the Manager.

Right-click the Manager with the Label Gun without sneaking to copy its source/dest table to the disk. Alternatively use empty-hand cable label editing on that Manager disk. Labels are case-sensitive and must match the preview.
Press Start. Each 20-tick run attempts to move items from source to dest. Check both chests; a full or inaccessible destination can leave items behind.
For printed values, enable Capture in Manager Terminal or a connected Studio Debug terminal. PRINT is separate from moving the items.

navigationRules.scope: Always show view, action, topic, result count, and removable filters. Switching By action/By topic changes the choices displayed, not the other active filter.
navigationRules.counts: Show counts for each opposite-axis choice before selecting it. Count Building blocks and Worked examples separately, exclude alias-only rows.
navigationRules.empty: No silent fallback. State both filters, keep the search text, and offer Clear action / Clear topic / Search all as separate explicit actions.
navigationRules.search: All whitespace-separated words must match, case-insensitively across name, summary, details, syntax aliases, player synonyms and named variants. Matching a variant selects/highlights that variant and its correct preview; divide must not open Add. Exact user function names remain case-sensitive when inserted.
navigationRules.narrow: A compact scope line and filter sheet replace twenty permanent buttons. Results wrap full distinct names. Details has Back and a scrollable variants list or form/direction controls. Preserve filters, query, result scroll, selected row, variant, and preview scroll.
navigationRules.topicVariants: Items/Fluids chooses the corresponding named resource-type variant. Legacy/typed syntax form is explicit. Placement badge and preview always describe the selected variant, not only its parent.
navigationRules.related: Dependency links can cross current filters only after an explicit Open related action, which shows the destination scope and preserves Back history.
navigationRules.safeInsert: Selecting a row or variant never edits source. Insert changes only the chosen range as one undoable operation, selects placeholders, and never changes the open program by selecting a whole-program example.
navigationRules.variantHelp: Selected variant fields override parent placement, inputs, result, help, topics, and preview. Only genuinely shared notes are inherited. Guide-only usage examples are never part of Insert.
navigationRules.searchAll: Search all explicitly clears action/topic filters and searches both Building blocks and Worked examples, with the cross-view scope visible. Back restores the previous scope. Topic-incompatible variants stay excluded until the player explicitly broadens the scope; multiple matching variants remain selectable and the chosen preview is named.
navigationRules.case: Discovery ignores case, but insertion preserves the exact case of player function names, label names, registry IDs, and OreDictionary names. Search never rewrites saved program identifiers.
navigationRules.topicCounts: Counts include a card only if it has a usable variant for the topic. All card counts exclude aliases and are computed separately per examples/blocks view.
navigationRules.previewEditing: The preview is read-only. Insert selects labelled placeholders for replacement in the editor. Named variants and documented comparison choices update the preview before insertion; literal sample resources must be replaced after Insert, in every line that uses them. A card must never claim an unimplemented resource picker or editable preview.

glossary.Label: A name you assign to one or more connected blocks on the running disk.
glossary.Trigger: A block that starts on a timer or an event.
glossary.Value: Data used by an instruction, such as a number or a true/false check.
glossary.Variable: A named stored value. Bare names must avoid reserved language words; new previews use descriptive names such as signalLevel and rightText. Existing $names remain accepted.
glossary.Snapshot: A saved reading of contents; it does not reserve resources and may become out of date.
glossary.Filter: A rule selecting resource types; it is not a physical item/fluid stack.
glossary.Exact key: Captured resource identity including NBT (and item metadata); amount is separate.
glossary.NBT: Extra item data, such as a custom name or stored heat.
glossary.Record/struct: Related values stored under fixed field names.
glossary.Array/list: An ordered sequence of values of one type.
glossary.Void procedure: A function that performs instructions without returning a value.
